quarterly_data.signal: Q2 FY2026 results: total revenue $168 million, 'in line with the midpoint of the guidance range we provided last quarter'. Power revenue $118 million, of which Mohawk Valley (the 200-millimeter device fab) contributed approximately $75 million, including some last-time-buy shipments from the Durham campus ahead of its closure; Materials revenue $50 million. Non-GAAP gross margin negative 34%, hurt by a $39 million fresh start accounting drag ($23 million of inventory step-ups), $14 million of specific inventory reserves and approximately $48 million of underutilization; adjusted EBITDA negative $82 million. CFO: revenue reflects 'a mix between a weaker automotive market and fast-growing mid to high voltage revenue', linked to traction in AI and data center.
quarterly_data.figure: $168 million revenue; Power $118 million (Mohawk Valley approximately $75 million); Materials $50 million; non-GAAP GM negative 34%; adjusted EBITDA negative $82 million

quarterly_data.signal: Materials revenue of $50 million was 'driven largely by a tightening demand environment and increased competition in the market'. Materials strategy is two-pronged: scale and strengthen 200-millimeter leadership for power devices today (priority is 'delivering high-quality 200-millimeter wafers at commercial scale', positioned to serve both the internal device roadmap and merchant demand) while advancing 300-millimeter capabilities. Materials capacity is already built in Durham and Siler City; CEO: 'The factories are built', production will be scaled up as demand picks up and depends on customer adoption of the technology.
quarterly_data.figure: Materials $50 million; 200-millimeter wafers at commercial scale

quarterly_data.signal: Wolfspeed 'recently produced a single crystal 300-millimeter silicon carbide wafer'. Management's view: 300-millimeter does not replace 200-millimeter for power devices in the near term but 'helps lay the groundwork for silicon carbide beyond power', using SiC's thermal conductivity and optical properties (example given: next-generation AR/VR systems). Asked by an analyst about SiC substrates in the AI data center, the CEO said there is 'clear interest to explore now to see is there a way to use this thermal conductor in some type of improvement for the system architecture' and 'very early ongoing discussions with key partners in the industry', but 'I cannot give you an exact timeline on revenue'.
quarterly_data.figure: single crystal 300-millimeter SiC wafer produced; no revenue timeline

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q3 FY2026 outlook (the transcript prints 'During 2026, we expect revenues between $140 million and $160 million' inside the CFO's fiscal-third-quarter outlook). The decline is driven primarily by accelerated customer purchases in the first fiscal quarter (customers building inventory with orders from the Durham fab before its planned closure), certain customers pursuing second sourcing of products, and weaker EV demand. OpEx expected flat to slightly down sequentially; no numeric gross-margin guide because of ongoing fresh start accounting impacts, but further quarter-over-quarter improvement is expected and gross margin is 'expected to remain negative in fiscal Q3'. AI data centers and other industrial and energy applications 'represent meaningful long-term growth drivers, but they will take time to scale and offset the continued softness in EVs'. An update on the long-range plan (long-term financial targets and capital allocation) is expected in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: revenues between $140 million and $160 million; gross margin to remain negative in fiscal Q3

quarterly_data.signal: Post-restructuring balance sheet: cash and short-term investments $1.3 billion; net debt of approximately $600 million; annual cash interest expense lowered by approximately 60%. Collected the upsized $700 million 48D cash tax refund in Q2 and used part of it to reduce $175 million of first lien debt; approximately 1.5 million shares were converted from the second lien convert (debt reduction of approximately $18 million); together $25 million in annual interest savings. CapEx was $31 million in Q2 (primarily prior commitments) versus approximately $400 million in the year-ago quarter and will be driven further down; non-GAAP operating expenses are $200 million lower on a run-rate basis versus last year; Q2 successor-period operating cash flow was negative $43 million. The first lien interest rate will step up around the middle of calendar year 2026 and management is actively looking at refinancing options (first lien and converts), probably not in a one-go transaction. CFIUS clearance released approximately 16.85 million new shares to Renesas under the restructuring agreement; total shares outstanding are now 45.1 million.
quarterly_data.figure: cash $1.3 billion; net debt approximately $600 million; $700 million 48D refund; $175 million first lien reduced; CapEx $31 million

players.product: 650V-10kV SiC power MOSFETs & modules (TOL D) for AI data center / SST

quarterly_data.signal: AI data center: 'we have doubled our data center revenue in the last three quarters, with 50% quarter-over-quarter growth from Q1 to Q2'; Wolfspeed devices are 'already embedded in critical AI data center power systems'. The company is 'actively collaborating with a broad ecosystem of partners to support the industry transition from legacy 400-volt architectures to next-generation 800-volt AI platforms'. AI data centers operate at significantly higher voltages than legacy data centers, and as voltages rise management expects a growing share of the addressable market 'from grid to rack' to be better served by SiC than by silicon.
quarterly_data.figure: data center revenue doubled in the last three quarters; 50% quarter-over-quarter growth from Q1 to Q2

quarterly_data.signal: CEO's AI data center socket map: rack power is 'round about the 100 kilowatt-ish per rack' today, 'moving in two years or so to, like, 600 kilowatt per rack into, like, a mega rack, like, the 2029, 2030 timeframe'. SiC targets span energy generation, energy storage systems, the move from traditional transformers to solid-state transformers ('That transition is starting to happen here'), the UPS ('a big, big application') and cooling (40% of the energy in the data center goes to cooling devices). Wolfspeed recently announced a new side cooling package to build products specifically for this application and reports 'multiple excellent customer engagements and partner engagements'.
quarterly_data.figure: 100 kilowatt-ish per rack today; 'moving in two years or so to, like, 600 kilowatt per rack into, like, a mega rack, like, the 2029, 2030 timeframe'; cooling 40% of data center energy

quarterly_data.signal: Completed the shutdown of all 150-millimeter device production at the Durham campus at the end of November, roughly one month ahead of schedule, moving the entire device platform to 200-millimeter manufacturing in Mohawk Valley; the closure improved gross margins by $5 million in the quarter, and end-of-life purchasing tied to the transition is finished. CEO: 'we are really the first company in the Western world who's completely only manufacturing the 200-millimeter devices.' Underutilization remains a headwind; the footprint spans North Carolina, Mohawk Valley and a device and module site in Arkansas.
quarterly_data.figure: 150-millimeter device production shut down one month ahead of schedule; gross margins improved by $5 million

quarterly_data.signal: Diversifying away from EVs (CEO: 'we're pretty much looking to pivot away from being a one-trick pony focused on EVs'): go-to-market reorganized around four verticals (auto, industrial energy, aerospace and defense, materials) with an application-oriented sales organization, key-account tiering, a distribution channel strategy and a US rep structure, staffed with hires from other big semiconductor companies. Industrial and energy focus: AI data center power, grid storage, solid-state transformers and grid modernization. Automotive stays core despite muted EV demand; Wolfspeed announced a partnership with Toyota to power the onboard charging systems for its BEVs and is sampling across several key strategic programs with top global EV OEMs. Customers value the US-based, vertically integrated footprint after certain countries restricted exports of materials such as gallium; the Department of Defense and Department of Energy have designated SiC a critical material.
